title: 1958 AHSME Problem 47
statement: \(ABCD\) is a rectangle (see the accompanying diagram) with \(P\) any point on \(\overline{AB}.\) \(PS\perp BD\) and \(PR\perp AC.\) \(AF\perp BD\) and \(PQ\perp AF.\) Then \(PR+PS\) is equal to:

solutions.text:
Since \(AF\perp BD\) and \(PQ\perp AF,\) we have \(PQ\parallel BD.\) Also \(PS\perp BD,\) so \(PS\parallel AF.\) Thus quadrilateral \(QPSF\) is a rectangle, and \[ PS=QF. \] Let \(T=PQ\cap AC.\) The diagonals of a rectangle make equal angles with side \(AB,\) so \(\angle PAT=\angle APT,\) giving \(AT=PT.\) The right triangles \(ATQ\) and \(PTR\) are similar because they share the angle at \(T.\) Since their hypotenuses \(AT\) and \(PT\) are equal, \(AQ=PR.\) Therefore \[ PR+PS=AQ+QF=AF. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Because \(PQ\parallel BD\) and \(PS\parallel AF,\) identify the small parallelogram near \(F\) and \(S\)
Use the intersection \(T=PQ\cap AC\) to compare the right triangles \(PTR\) and \(ATQ\)
